item.text: I’m synthesizing from the already gathered 2024 source set rather than widening the search further. For 3B.1 the key question is whether there is any direct evidence of abuse prevention or accountability, and the record looks thin.

# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 3B.1 evidence note

Bottom line: **evidence is sparse and mostly negative-adjacent**. I found **no strong 2024 evidence** that Sharif actively protected residents from state violence, torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, extrajudicial killing, or arbitrary punishment. The clearest available materials instead show a coercive political environment and heavy reliance on security forces, though some counterterrorism actions were framed through consensus and formal institutions rather than open-ended repression.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|

This is the best available evidence that security force mobilization was channeled through formal, collective authority rather than ad hoc abuse. | 3B.1; also 2B.8 |
| Mixed / slightly favorable | Civil, Military leadership reiterate commitment to work together for prosperous, secure Pakistan | Radio Pakistan | 2024-03-15 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/15-03-2024/civil-military-leadership-reiterate-commitment-to-work-together-for-prosperous-secure-pakistan | Sharif said the government would provide all resources required for operational readiness after briefings on the security environment and counterterrorism operations. This supports a reading of state force being tied to articulated security needs, but it does not show protection from abuse or accountability for abuses. | 3B.1; also 2B.8 |
| Negative / strong | Pakistan election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty condemned the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of coercive state conduct around Sharif’s ascent and cuts against a clean protection/accountability reading. | 3B.1; also 2B.6, 2B.10 |
| Negative-adjacent | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | In the same UNGA speech that urged dialogue, Sharif also warned Pakistan would “respond most decisively” to Indian aggression and described India’s doctrine in nuclearized terms. That does not show domestic repression, but it does reflect a broader coercive political style rather than a strong restraint/accountability signal. | 3B.1; also 2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.6 |
| Negative-adjacent | PM voices satisfaction over Pakistan Army’s operational preparedness | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-05 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/05-09-2024/pm-expresses-satisfaction-over-pak-armys-operational-preparedness | Sharif praised operational preparedness and said the deterrence regime would impose costs on any adversary. This is not proof of abuse, but it shows continued comfort with force-centered state power rather than explicit protection of civilians from it. | 3B.1; also 2B.8, 1B.5 |

## Synthesis

- Best-supported conclusion: **I could not find direct evidence that Sharif protected residents from state violence or held security forces accountable for abuses in 2024.**
- The strongest contrary signal is the **election-day internet shutdown**, which Amnesty treated as a rights violation.
- The closest positive evidence is that counterterrorism mobilization was presented as **consensus-based** and formally authorized, but that is only indirect and does not establish protection from torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, or extrajudicial killing.
- Confidence should remain **low**, because the 2024 record available here is mostly about broad security policy, not documented abuse investigations or accountability actions.

## Search gap

- I did **not** find a reliable 2024 source showing Sharif ordered investigations, prosecutions, or discipline for torture, disappearances, extrajudicial killings, or political imprisonment.
- I also did **not** find direct reporting on his response to specific abuses by police, intelligence services, or paramilitaries.
- So the evidence base is thin and leans negative by omission: there is no strong accountability story in the material surfaced here.
